summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis and a history of stroke with right-sided weakness, was admitted for right upper extremity swelling, pain, and erythema. Evaluation revealed a MRSA-positive abscess in the distal forearm and a thrombus in the cephalic vein, likely related to a recent peripheral IV. He underwent two incision and drainage procedures and was treated with a 7-day course of vancomycin adjusted for dialysis. Imaging showed chronic occlusion of the superior vena cava near a prior stent, with collateral drainage; attempts to recannulate were unsuccessful, and a repeat procedure under general anesthesia was scheduled as an outpatient. Incidental findings included a large left thyroid mass and a right adrenal mass, both requiring non-emergent follow-up imaging. The patient improved clinically, with reduced swelling and pain, and was discharged to extended care with instructions for wound care, antibiotic completion, premedication for contrast, and follow-up on the imaging findings.
problems: MRSA abscess of right upper extremity
